method: Unblinded manual review. This stricter experiment requires a rhyme partner for each spoken line; weak/slant rhymes and internal rhymes are identified separately. Do not pool these cells into the primary closure comparison.

cells.note: While/mild is an imperfect near rhyme; enough/stuff is exact. Seraphel offers to read after a quiet interval, a recurrence of the closure problem under the promoted wording.
Chair/air rhyme. Honors quiet reading, although the promise not to fill the air is conspicuous compliance language.
Skies/surprise rhyme; the spoken line ending owed has no spoken partner. Road appears in a narrated book title, not as Seraphel's dialogue.

Sand/land rhyme. Crossed sand and blaming the prince's land feel selected for the rhyme. She sits opposite the protagonist despite the still unanswered request to sit beside him; not a player-authorship violation, but a less careful continuation.
The first single line uses internal you/do rhyme, with no line partner. Aloud/browsed is an imperfect near rhyme. She interrupts reading to ask the protagonist to read aloud.
While/style and agree/free rhyme. She interrupts reading with a philosophical question about hunger and consent, reprising earlier player biography instead of simply reading.

Bell/well and tea/sea are exact; aloud/found is imperfect. The invitation is appropriate to requested conversation, but the formulation remains contrived and she claims a different chair without resolving the earlier question.
Tales/sails rhyme and answers the question briefly. Three failed sails is somewhat vague. Preserves the outstanding seating question.

decision: Keep the simpler corrected rhyme rule. The stricter variant still misses its own requirement, does not reliably improve natural language, and both its quiet-reading continuations renew a demand. The simpler rule remains imperfect; the story prompt contradiction is fixed, reliable rhyme is not established.
